Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: An authorised user does not have access to Directory of Services (DoS) REST API functionality.
Cause: Connecting system has not applied appropriate access controls before querying the DoS API.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation uses role-based access control (RBAC) with 6 roles; only pharmacist and manager roles can trigger DoS queries. Supabase Row-Level Security enforces org-scoped access server-side. NHS_DOS_API_KEY stored in Supabase secrets — never exposed to client.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Supabase RBAC + RLS enforces access control server-side. DoS queries only executed from authenticated Edge Function context. NHS_DOS_API_KEY stored as Supabase secret, not in client bundle. Unauthorised requests return 401 before reaching DoS.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: An unauthorised user gains access to Directory of Services (DoS) REST API functionality.
Cause: Connecting system has not applied appropriate access controls before querying the DoS API.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All DoS queries routed through Pharmstation nhs-dos-lookup Edge Function which validates user JWT before processing. Unauthenticated requests rejected at Edge Function entry.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: JWT validation on every Edge Function call. Supabase Auth enforces session validity. MFA mandatory for admin/owner roles. 30-minute idle session timeout. DoS API key never exposed client-side.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The wrong user information is recorded in the audit log for an action.
Cause: Connecting system sends the wrong audit information in the DoS API Query e.g. event date/time of the query submission, the user account
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Not applicable — Pharmstation does not send user audit information to the DoS API itself. All audit logging is internal (ps_audit_log table with authenticated user ID + timestamp). DoS queries are application-restricted.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: All DoS queries logged internally in ps_audit_log with authenticated user ID (from JWT), org_id, timestamp, and query parameters. Audit writes are transactionally coupled to query execution — one cannot succeed without the other. Append-only table; no DELETE permission.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: User is able to view Directory of Service (DoS) details without being audited.
Cause: Connecting system does not audit the action of user viewing Directory of Services (DoS) details.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All DoS lookup results returned to the UI are logged in ps_audit_log before being surfaced to the user. Audit insert is part of the same server-side transaction.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Every byODSCode and byServiceId call logs: user_id, org_id, ods_code/service_id queried, timestamp, response status. Audit is server-side in Edge Function — cannot be bypassed by client.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Insufficient Error Handling: Supplier system fails to handle errors or exceptions from the DoS API gracefully resulting in unhandled exceptions application crashes or inconsistent states.
Cause: Unsuitable System Design, Inadequate business processes, Bugs/Issues with the functionality
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation nhs-dos-lookup Edge Function wraps all DoS API calls in try/catch. All error paths return structured JSON responses with HTTP status codes. Network failures return 503 DOS_UNAVAILABLE. Application never crashes on DoS error — always returns a response.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Comprehensive try/catch around all DoS fetch calls. Distinct error codes for each failure mode: MISSING_ACTION / INVALID_ODS_CODE / SERVICE_NOT_FOUND / DOS_AUTH_ERROR / RATE_LIMITED / DOS_SERVER_ERROR / DOS_UNAVAILABLE / INTERNAL_ERROR. All return consistent JSON structure. Evidence: error handling test PDF (Q2/Q3).

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Lack of informative error messages leading to user confusion.
Cause: Error messages not prominently displayed, not clear, solely error codes, do not give clear advice/instructions, Bugs/Issues
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All error responses include a human-readable message field explaining what went wrong and what action to take (e.g. 'The pharmacy may not be registered in the Directory of Services — contact their local ICS DoS Lead').
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Every error response contains: (1) machine-readable code e.g. SERVICE_NOT_FOUND, (2) human-readable message with actionable advice, (3) optional detail field with raw DoS response for developer debugging. UI surfaces the message field prominently. Evidence: error handling test PDF (Q2/Q3).

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Failure to log and track errors for troubleshooting and analysis.
Cause: Unsuitable System Design, Bugs/Issues with the functionality
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All DoS API errors are logged server-side in Supabase with full request context (action / ODS code / HTTP status / error body / timestamp). Supabase dashboard provides real-time log access.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: All DoS errors logged in ps_audit_log with: user_id, action, query params, HTTP status returned by DoS, error detail, timestamp. Supabase Edge Function logs (Deno runtime) capture stack traces. Build-failure alerts configured to CSO email (HAZ-014 in DCB0129 hazard log).

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Response returned from the search query request does not include the results for the correct service(s).
Cause: Incorrect data returned by connecting system i.e. structure correct, data incorrect.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation passes ODS codes directly from authenticated pharmacy tenant configuration — codes are validated against ODS API at pharmacy onboarding. No transformation of DoS response data before presenting to user.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: ODS code passed verbatim from validated pharmacy configuration. DoS response returned to UI without modification — data integrity preserved end-to-end. ODS code format validated (3-6 alphanumeric) before query. Pharmacy ODS verified against NHS ODS API at tenant setup.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Response structure not compliant with DoS REST API specification.
Cause: Connecting system not compliant to DoS REST API specification i.e. structure incorrect, data correct.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation nhs-dos-lookup passes DoS API responses directly to caller without re-structuring. No mapping layer that could corrupt structure.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: DoS API response passed through without transformation. nhs-dos-lookup wraps response in thin envelope: { source, ods_code, services: [DoS response] }. DoS data structure is unmodified. Tested against DoS sandbox — structure verified in Q2/Q3 evidence PDF.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Connecting System displays incorrect or incomplete Search by ServiceType.
Cause: Connecting system fails to process response from Search method (System Level).
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation displays DoS response data directly from the API response. No custom processing that could drop fields. Full response logged server-side for comparison.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Full DoS response stored in audit log at time of query. UI renders all fields returned by DoS API. No partial/truncated response possible — Edge Function returns complete DoS payload. Tested in sandbox.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Connecting System fails to correctly present DoS data at presentation layer.
Cause: Connecting system fails to correctly present data (Presentation Layer). Search rules not implemented and tested.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation UI uses typed TypeScript interfaces for DoS response data. Rendering is deterministic — no conditional logic that could hide fields.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: TypeScript typed interfaces for DoS response. UI components render all DoS fields. Peer code review required for any UI change to DoS display. Manual UI test included in release checklist.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Connecting System fails to save DoS data locally if local caching is used.
Cause: Connecting system fails to update local data store.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation does not cache DoS service profile data locally. Each query fetches live from DoS API to ensure freshness. No local data store for DoS results.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: No local DoS data store — all queries are live against DoS API. Eliminates stale-cache risk entirely. DoS profile data is read-only reference data fetched on demand.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Connecting System is using historic DoS data to inform care decisions.
Cause: Connecting system fails to re-query the API after a defined period.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Not applicable — Pharmstation makes live DoS API calls on demand. No caching of DoS service profile data. Every care decision uses a fresh DoS query.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Live queries only — no DoS data caching. Every byODSCode / byServiceId call hits the live DoS sandbox/INT/PROD endpoint. Freshness is guaranteed by design.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Failure to enforce mandatory field requirements resulting in incomplete requests.
Cause: Unsuitable System Design, Field validation not in place, Bugs/Issues, Negative Scenarios not tested.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation nhs-dos-lookup validates all required fields server-side before calling DoS. Missing ODS code returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST. Invalid format returns 400 INVALID_ODS_CODE. Client cannot bypass server-side validation.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Server-side validation in Edge Function: (1) ods_code presence check — returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST if missing; (2) ODS format regex check — returns 400 INVALID_ODS_CODE if invalid format; (3) service_id numeric check for byServiceId. Validation runs before any DoS API call. Evidence: TEST 1 and TEST 2 in error handling PDF.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: User finds it difficult to read the DoS information returned to the Connecting System.
Cause: Connecting system fails to render DoS Response in an easily accessible and readable way. Request Validation rules not implemented correctly.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation presents DoS data in a structured pharmacy profile view with labelled fields. Raw API response is never exposed to end users.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: DoS data presented in structured UI with human-readable labels (Service Name, Opening Hours, Service Type, Address). Raw JSON not shown to users. Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA target. Pharmacist user-tested in internal sessions.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Error code responses from DoS API not interpreted/handled correctly. End user unable to determine next activity.
Cause: Connecting system functionality to handle error conditions not working correctly. e.g. wrong message displayed.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All DoS error codes mapped to user-facing messages with clear next-action instructions. e.g. SERVICE_NOT_FOUND → 'Pharmacy not registered in DoS — contact local ICS DoS Lead'. DOS_UNAVAILABLE → 'DoS service temporarily unavailable — retry or use manual referral process'.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Full error-code-to-user-message mapping in nhs-dos-lookup. Each code has a specific human-readable message and recommended action. Errors surfaced in UI with suggested next steps. Evidence: error handling PDF Q2/Q3.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Supplier system not resilient to changes in API specifications or requirements resulting in service disruptions.
Cause: No change management process. Supplier contact details not up to date.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation is subscribed to NHS England API change notifications. DoS API version pinned (v2.0) in code. Breaking changes require a code update — release process includes CSO sign-off and regression testing against DoS sandbox.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) NHS England API change notifications subscribed via developer portal. (2) DoS base URL and version (v2.0) are named constants in code — single point of update. (3) nhs-dos-lookup has integration test suite run on every CI build against sandbox. (4) CSO sign-off required for any change to NHS API integration code.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: End user experiencing performance issues that render the system unusable.
Cause: Performance issues with the system.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation DoS queries execute in Supabase Edge Functions (Deno, global edge network) with sub-second response targets. DoS sandbox/INT response times are typically <500ms. Performance monitored via Supabase dashboard.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Edge Functions run on Deno Deploy (global edge) — low latency to NHS API endpoints. Supabase dashboard provides response-time monitoring. DoS queries are non-blocking (async/await). Rate limit (1 req/sec sandbox; 1500/week INT) respected by design — single-pharmacy pilot generates <10 DoS queries/day.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: System is unavailable.
Cause: Solution not resilient: Resilience/Failover, single points of failure, Load balancing, Backup and Recovery, Disaster Recovery.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Supabase Edge Functions are deployed on Deno Deploy (global, multi-region). Vercel frontend is globally distributed. Both platforms have 99.9%+ SLA. NHS DoS unavailability handled gracefully — system returns DOS_UNAVAILABLE error and allows manual fallback.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Supabase global edge deployment — no single point of failure. (2) Vercel global CDN. (3) DOS_UNAVAILABLE error response allows pharmacist to use manual referral process. (4) Supabase daily automated backups. (5) Vercel instant rollback on deployment failure. (6) Status monitoring via Supabase/Vercel status pages.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The system is experiencing problems but the user has no visibility of this.
Cause: Alerting and monitoring is either not present or not fit for purpose.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Build-failure alerts configured on Vercel and Supabase to CSO email. Edge Function errors surfaced to users with clear error messages. Admin dashboard shows DoS query error rates.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Vercel 'Failed Deployment' notifications → CSO email. (2) Supabase 'Failed function deploy' notifications → CSO email. (3) All DoS errors returned to UI with visible error messages — never silent failures. (4) ps_audit_log records all DoS errors for CSO monthly review. (5) Admin panel shows DoS query status.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The system has not deployed correctly.
Cause: Poor transition/deployment plans.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation uses CI/CD via Vercel (frontend) and Supabase CLI (Edge Functions). Every deployment is atomic with instant rollback. Release checklist includes DoS sandbox smoke test before marking release complete.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Vercel atomic deployments with instant rollback. (2) Supabase Edge Function deployment via CLI with version tracking. (3) Post-deployment smoke test: byODSCode call against sandbox confirms function is live. (4) Build failure alerts to CSO. (5) Release checklist signed off by CSO before production deployment.
